_meta: DRAFT — NOT YET IMPORTED (wired automatically by the gen-slices auto-loader). Africa-branch municipal-fiscal-tier push, round AF/G.23, 2026-08-13. Continues Mauritius beyond the wave-2 corpus (af-mauritius.json, national CPI + Rodrigues Regional Assembly Act only) into the municipal/district/Rodrigues fiscal-transfer tier. Mints the Local Government Act 2011's statutory grant-formula clause (Section 83), the Ministry of Local Government and Disaster Risk Management's own Annual Report 2023-2024 (naming the Municipal Council of Port Louis and the District Council of Grand Port with Rs figures), the Municipal City Council of Port Louis's own IPSAS-compliant audited financial statements (FY2017-2018, showing Government Grants as its largest single revenue source), and two National Audit Office annual audit reports on the Rodrigues Regional Assembly (FY2014 and FY2019-20) quantifying the central-government-grant-to-RRA dependency chain across a multi-year time series. No dedicated NAO audit-report series exists for any of the 5 municipal/town councils (confirmed against NAO's own index page) — municipal councils instead publish their own annual reports, as Port Louis does. Two existing af-mauritius.json nodes (mu-statsmauritius-cpi, mu-rodrigues-regional-assembly-act-2001) were separately enriched in place this round with UPDATE-prefixed description text — see that file's own diff, not repeated here.

reports.title: Local Government Act 2011 (Act No. 36 of 2011), Section 83 — Grants to Municipal City Council, Municipal Town Council or District Council
reports.publisher: Attorney-General's Office, Mauritius (Revised Laws of Mauritius)
reports.description: Mauritius's national local-government statute, as consolidated in the Revised Laws of Mauritius (page marked "L18 – 52"). Section 83, "Grants to Municipal City Council, Municipal Town Council or District Council": "(1) (a) In every financial year, there shall be paid to the Municipal City Council, a Municipal Town Council or a District Council a grant from the Consolidated Fund of an amount calculated according to such formula as may be prescribed. (b) The formula for the payment of grants under this section shall operate for such period and on such conditions as may be prescribed." This is the enabling statutory clause — a Consolidated-Fund grant per a prescribed formula — not a document naming a specific council or a dollar figure; Sections 84 ("Release of grants") and 85 ("Annual estimates") are companion provisions. Sections 132–133 ("Obligation to prepare financial statements" / "Contents and form of financial statements") separately require every local authority other than a Village Council to produce audited financial statements within 3 months of the financial year end, and are the statutory basis the Municipal City Council of Port Louis cites for its own annual report (see mu-portlouis-citycouncil-annualreport-2017-18).
reports.cadence_note: One-off foundational legal instrument, currently in force per the Revised Laws version fetched.

reports.title: Ministry of Local Government and Disaster Risk Management — Annual Report 2023-2024
reports.publisher: Ministry of Local Government and Disaster Risk Management, Mauritius
reports.description: The Ministry's own annual report, Section 6.4 "Grant to Local Authorities (Recurrent Expenditures)" (page 41): "During the course of the year and following the midterm review exercise, Councils were provided with additional Grant-In-Aid to the tune of Rs. 215 M to enable them to maintain their level of activities. Moreover, funds to the tune of Rs 10.5M have been released to the Municipal Council of Port Louis for payment to Victoria Station Ltd (VSL) and compensation to Pick N Eat Rs 4.6 M. Rs 7.4 M to the District Council of Grand Port to meet its obligations towards Arbitration for Mahebourg Market." Companion data from Sections 6.1–6.3 (pages 37, 40): Vote 5-1 "Local Government" was budgeted at Rs 5,364,000,000 for FY2023-2024 (Rs 4,494,600,000 recurrent / Rs 869,400,000 capital), and "Grants Recurrent (Local Authorities)" made up 85.64% of the Ministry's Vote 5-1 actual expenditure per the report's own pie chart. Only the Municipal Council of Port Louis and the District Council of Grand Port are named individually with Rs figures in this document; Beau Bassin-Rose Hill, Curepipe, Quatre Bornes, and Vacoas-Phoenix are not individually named with figures here.

reports.title: City Council of Port Louis — Annual Report and Financial Statements for the year ended 30 June 2018
reports.publisher: Municipal City Council of Port Louis (MCCPL)
reports.description: The City Council of Port Louis's own IPSAS-compliant audited financial statements, hosted on its own domain (mccpl.mu). Self-description: "The City Council of Port Louis is a corporate body established under the Local Government Act 2011, Part II Section 3 and 7. The Council was established in 1830 by Ordinance No 16," and "The financial statements of the City Council of Port Louis have been prepared in compliance with Section 132 and 133 of the Local Government Act 2011 and the International Public Sector Accounting Standards (IPSAS), with effect from 1st July 2017." Statement of Financial Performance for the year ended 30 June 2018 (report page 62): "Revenue from non-exchange transactions ... Government Grants [Note] 21 580,311,863 ... Total Revenue 867,532,015." Note 21 "Government Grants" breakdown (report page 84): "Grant in Aid 570,777,098 / Grant Rodent Control 1,279,992 / Grant Family Day 622,675 / National Day Celebration 1,320,837 / Water bills 407,430 / Cyclone Berguitta 587,489 / Pay clerk fees 37,192 / Trainee Engineer Scheme 329,890 ... Total Government Grants 580,311,863." Government Grants (66.9% of Total Revenue) are Port Louis's largest single revenue category, with the "Grant in Aid" line alone exceeding Property Taxes (Rs 129,398,203) and Trade Fees (Rs 93,746,400) combined.
reports.cadence_note: Annual audited financial statements (FY2017-2018 edition; the most recent MCCPL annual report found hosted on the council's own site as of this research round — not necessarily the newest possible edition).

reports.title: National Audit Office — Audit Report on the Accounts of the Rodrigues Regional Assembly, 2014
reports.description: Section 2.5.1 "Financial Allocation to RRA" (page 9): "In September 2013, Government approved a budget allocation to RRA in the sum of Rs 1,950 million, comprising Rs 1,550 million for recurrent grant and Rs 400 million for capital grant. The actual amount of grant received was Rs 2,170,913,800, including an amount of Rs 220,913,800 as additional contribution from the Programme 311- 'Rodrigues Development' of the Prime Minister's Office. Revenue collected by the RRA amounted to Rs 25,356,042, thus bringing total revenue to Rs 2,196,269,842." This documents RRA's FY2014 revenue as roughly 99% central-government grant (Rs 2,170,913,800 of Rs 2,196,269,842 total), compositely sourced from a general Government budget allocation plus a specifically named Prime Minister's Office programme line (Programme 311, "Rodrigues Development").
reports.cadence_note: Annual audit report (FY2014 edition); part of NAO's dedicated Rodrigues Regional Assembly report series (confirmed via NAO's own audit-report index — see _dropped).

reports.title: National Audit Office — Audit Report on the Accounts of the Rodrigues Regional Assembly, 2019-20
reports.description: Section 2.3 "Rodrigues Consolidated Fund (RCF) - Transfer from RCF to cater for Shortfall" (page 14): "RRA received a grant of some Rs 3,898 million from the Central Government in 2019-20. Revenue totalling some Rs 38 million were collected by the RRA, bringing the total inflow to some Rs 3,936 million. Total expenditure for 2019-20 amounted to Rs 3,955 million. Some Rs 20.9 million were transferred from RCF to cater for the shortfall." A three-year "Government Grant" comparison table in the same section: "3,681,490,778 [2019-20] / 3,575,000,000 [2018-19] / 3,425,000,000 [2017-18]" with corresponding "Additional Contribution 216,490,000 / 30,000,000 / -". Section 4.2, "Detailed Statement of Revenue of the Rodrigues Consolidated Fund" (Table 4, in Rs million): "Government Grant 3,897.98 [2019-20] / 3,605.00 [2018-19] / 3,425.00 [2017-18]," with: "Revenue of the RRA comprises principally of Grants/Contributions from the Central Government and internally generated revenue which consists of receipts from licence fees, social contributions, property income, sales of goods and services, incidental sales by non-market establishment, miscellaneous sales of goods and services, fines and miscellaneous revenue." CAVEAT: the report itself flags an internal accounting inconsistency — "An inconsistent accounting treatment of the item 'Grant - Contribution from Central Government'... The total Grants figure was wrongly stated as Rs 3,918,936,526" — a Rs 20,955,748 discrepancy between how the grant vs. RCF-transfer figures were classified in RRA's own accounts that year; the exact-rupee Table 2 figure (Rs 3,681,490,778) and the Table 4 Rs-million figure (3,897.98M, which appears inclusive of the Additional Contribution) do not reconcile cleanly and both should be treated as reported by the auditors rather than as a single unambiguous total.
reports.cadence_note: Annual audit report (FY2019-20 edition, includes FY2018-19 and FY2017-18 comparatives); part of NAO's dedicated Rodrigues Regional Assembly report series (confirmed via NAO's own audit-report index — see _dropped).

dependencies.basis: The Ministry's Annual Report 2023-2024 documents actual Grant-in-Aid disbursements (Rs 215M additional grant-in-aid; Rs 10.5M to the Municipal Council of Port Louis; Rs 7.4M to the District Council of Grand Port) that are payments under the same Consolidated-Fund grant-to-local-authorities mechanism the Local Government Act 2011's Section 83 establishes ("there shall be paid to the Municipal City Council, a Municipal Town Council or a District Council a grant from the Consolidated Fund of an amount calculated according to such formula as may be prescribed"). The Annual Report does not cite Section 83 by number, so this is recorded as a general institutional cites relationship rather than a stronger calculation dependency.

Port Louis's own financial statements state directly: "The financial statements of the City Council of Port Louis have been prepared in compliance with Section 132 and 133 of the Local Government Act 2011 and the International Public Sector Accounting Standards (IPSAS), with effect from 1st July 2017" — a direct 'our preparation methodology IS mandated by this Act' claim, naming the same Act (Local Government Act 2011) that mu-lga-2011-s83-grants represents.

The NAO's audit report is on the accounts of the Rodrigues Regional Assembly, the body established by and operating under the Rodrigues Regional Assembly Act 2001, and its Section 2.5.1 quantifies the central-government grant that funds RRA's budget within the statutory framework (the Rodrigues Consolidated Fund, Section 42 of the Act) that mu-rodrigues-regional-assembly-act-2001 quotes. The 2014 report does not cite the Act or the RCF by name in the quoted passage, so this is recorded as a general institutional cites relationship.

The report's own Section 2.3 heading names the fund directly — "Rodrigues Consolidated Fund (RCF) - Transfer from RCF to cater for Shortfall" — and Section 4.2 is titled "Detailed Statement of Revenue of the Rodrigues Consolidated Fund," both reporting on the same Rodrigues Consolidated Fund that Section 42 of the Rodrigues Regional Assembly Act 2001 establishes ("There shall be a Rodrigues Consolidated Fund which shall consist of...", quoted in mu-rodrigues-regional-assembly-act-2001). The report quantifies the fund's central-government-grant inflows across three fiscal years but does not cite the Act by number, so this is recorded as cites rather than a stronger calculation dependency.

_dropped.edge: mu-statsmauritius-cpi -> IMF CPI Manual / ILO CPI Manual (specific titled methodology document)
_dropped.why: Statistics Mauritius's own CPI technical notes (both the 2022-dated and 2026-dated editions) credit only generic "ILO and SADC recommendations," never naming a specific titled manual. Two plausible specific targets were identified but not fetched/verified this round: the IMF's own CPI Manual (imf.org/-/media/files/data/cpi/cpi-manual-concepts-and-methods-white-cover-version.pdf) and the ILO's CPI Manual (ilo.org .../wcms_331153.pdf). Neither was force-linked as the specifically-intended document since Statistics Mauritius's own text does not name either by title. Flagged as an open lead for a future round.

_dropped.edge: individual municipal-council NAO audit reports (Port Louis, Beau Bassin-Rose Hill, Curepipe, Quatre Bornes, Vacoas-Phoenix)
_dropped.why: The National Audit Office's own audit-report index (nao.govmu.org/nao/index.php/annualauditreport/, fetched successfully) lists only two entities with dedicated report series: "Government of Mauritius" and "Rodrigues Regional Assembly." No separate audit-report series exists for any of the 5 Municipal City/Town Councils or for District Councils on the NAO's own site structure. Municipal councils instead publish their own annual reports on their own council websites, as confirmed for Port Louis (mu-portlouis-citycouncil-annualreport-2017-18).
